happened: Section 702 was set to expire in April 2026. Congress passed two short extensions, to April 30 and then June 12, 2026, but the House failed to pass a longer renewal. The law's authority lapsed on June 12, 2026, for the first time since 2008. A court approval issued earlier lets the program keep running until March 2027.

key_dates.event: Congress extends Section 702 to April 30, 2026 (H.R. 8322).
Congress extends Section 702 to June 12, 2026 (S. 4465).
House rejects a longer renewal (H.R. 9238).
Section 702 authority lapses.

legal: No court ruling. The Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court approved the program's yearly certifications in March 2026, which reportedly allow it to continue until March 2027.
closeness: The recommendation was to keep Section 702 and let Congress weigh reforms. Congress debated reforms, including warrant rules, and kept the law alive briefly, but did not renew it, so the statute lapsed.
uncertain: The project's copy of every law passed by the 119th Congress (through October 20, 2026) contains only the two short extensions (P.L. 119-84 and P.L. 119-87) and no later renewal; news searches found none either. I did not check what Congress did with the privacy board's 2023 report. Newest source: June 2026.

happened: In April 2025, CNN reported that the administration had tightly limited who receives the President's Daily Brief. At first White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles personally approved each person with access; later DNI Tulsi Gabbard took over that decision.

key_dates.event: CNN reports tight limits on who receives the President's Daily Brief.

closeness: This matches the chapter's call for much narrower distribution and a review of who gets the brief.
uncertain: The recipient list is classified, so the number of recipients is not public. Details come from news reports citing unnamed officials. Newest source: April 2025.

sources.label: Trump administration has tightly restricted access to president's daily intelligence brief

happened: In May 2025, DNI Tulsi Gabbard moved the staff who produce the President's Daily Brief from CIA headquarters to the ODNI campus, Fox News reported. The same week she also moved the National Intelligence Council.

key_dates.event: Daily Brief staff physically moved from CIA to ODNI.

closeness: Moving Daily Brief staff to ODNI matches half of the chapter's idea. No report was found on whether briefers now come from agencies other than the CIA.
uncertain: Whether the staff were formally transferred or only relocated, and who now delivers the brief, are not confirmed. Details come from news reports. Newest source: May 2025.

sources.label: Gabbard moves presidential daily intelligence brief staff from CIA to ODNI

happened: The August 2025 "ODNI 2.0" fact sheet said DNI Tulsi Gabbard told the Intelligence Advanced Research Projects Activity (IARPA) to invest in solutions to near-term gaps in the intelligence community rather than long-term concepts. It also said the DNI issued guidance to speed purchases of commercially available technology.

key_dates.event: ODNI 2.0 fact sheet describes new direction for IARPA.

closeness: Leaning on commercial technology fits the chapter's wish not to duplicate private-sector work. But the chapter wants research focused on hard problems, while the new direction stresses near-term needs. No change at the CIA's science and technology directorate was found.
uncertain: Which IARPA programs changed is not public. Newest source: August 2025.
